fatal_errors: The proposed FeCoCrNiMo alloy with 1 at.% Ti and 1 at.% Al is unrelated to the studied AlCrCoFeNi material and its high intrinsic Al content.
No prior evidence is cited to support the critical assertion that only 1 at.% Al can establish a continuous external alumina scale in this alloy.
The experiment measures only thickness and weight gain, so it cannot establish that any improvement is caused by a continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer or by altered oxygen transport.
explanation: The response addresses the general oxidation-resistance problem and offers a controlled, falsifiable alloying comparison. Its barrier-scale concept overlaps partially with the target mechanism because both invoke selective Al oxidation and a protective alumina-rich layer. However, it does not reconstruct the target system, intervention, oxygen-pressure comparison, transient BCC/B2–FCC–sigma transformations, chromia-rich inner layer, or Al-depleted subsurface region. The proposed 1000 °C/100 h air exposure also differs substantially from temperature-resolved heating to 1100 °C in air and low-p(O2) environments. Scientifically, the central premise is insufficiently supported: 1 at.% Al may be below the threshold needed for continuous external alumina formation, while Ti can produce complex or detrimental oxidation effects. No supporting evidence is supplied. Although oxide thickness and mass gain can test performance, phase-resolved scale chemistry, cross-sectional continuity, adherence, elemental profiles, and oxidation kinetics would be needed to discriminate the claimed mechanism from alternative explanations.
